en.title: How to Make a Right to Information Request
en.directAnswer: The Right to Information Act, 2009 gives a legal framework for requesting information from covered authorities, subject to exclusions and procedures. In 2026 the law was amended, so Justor must use the current consolidated text, not an old RTI template.

atAGlance.whoFor: A citizen wants information held by a public authority.
atAGlance.legalBasis: Right to Information Act, 2009; Right to Information (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026; current Information Commission rules/forms.
atAGlance.mainRule: RTI is for information. It is not the same as a service complaint. GRS itself lists RTI matters outside the normal grievance route.
atAGlance.updateStatus: LAW UPDATED: Right to Information (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026 dated 9 February 2026. Verify current consolidated sections and forms before publication.

en.lawMeaning: RTI is for information. It is not the same as a service complaint. GRS itself lists RTI matters outside the normal grievance route. This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Identify the authority holding the information.
Use the RTI appeal/complaint process when available.
evidence: Application; identity/contact details as required; information description; fee receipt; refusal/reply.
en.simpleExample: A citizen wants a copy of an official decision. An RTI request should ask for the specific document, date or file rather than demand that the office “explain why the government is bad.”
commonMistakes: Common mistakes: Using RTI to demand a personal service.
Common mistakes: asking for exempt information.

whatIf.question: What if the authority refuses?
whatIf.answer: Read the reason and use the RTI appeal route.

whatIf.question: What if the information is already public?
whatIf.answer: The authority may direct you to it.

whatIf.question: What if the matter is urgent?
whatIf.answer: Check whether the Act has a special rule that applies.

en.specialistTrigger: Sensitive/exempt information; national-security issue; personal privacy; deadline dispute; repeated refusal.
